deckTitle: Plato's Dungeon Raid — Full Class Roster v05

cards.power: You pick the class with no spells and no gimmick. You hit things with a sword.
cards.lore: Every party needs the one who read none of the rulebook and still showed up on time.
cards.gradeReason: Instantly embodiable — you ARE this person at every table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: armored rhino fighter at dungeon entrance, reading no rulebook. Mood: cheerfully oblivious.

cards.power: You catch your breath mid-fight. You are somehow still standing.
cards.lore: The fighter's superpower is not dying when everyone had already written him off.
cards.gradeReason: Pure survival performance — every table has this fighter.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: battered rhino fighter exhaling steam mid-combat, enemies swarming. Mood: defiant, impossible.

cards.power: You take two turns in one. Nobody questions how.
cards.lore: While the casters debated the lore, the fighter solved the problem. Twice.
cards.gradeReason: Double-turn is the purest fighter fantasy — immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: rhino fighter blurring with two sword swings simultaneously. Mood: kinetic, decisive.

cards.power: You did the most damage all campaign. No one noticed.
cards.lore: The class with no story is the one the story could not happen without.
cards.gradeReason: Strong lore but observational — describes a feeling more than a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: rhino fighter on pile of defeated foes, surrounded by peacock bard taking credit. Mood: understated glory.

cards.power: You rage. You go in first. You ask questions never.
cards.lore: Every barbarian's first session begins with a door that did not need breaking.
cards.gradeReason: Three words: rage, go, never. Instant character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink red-wash. Subject: honey badger barbarian smashing an innocent door, party wincing behind. Mood: gleeful destruction.

cards.power: You trade your defense for damage. You consider this a good deal.
cards.lore: The barbarian found the button that makes the numbers bigger. The barbarian presses the button.
cards.gradeReason: Button-presser is a universal performance everyone knows and loves.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink red-wash. Subject: orc barbarian gleefully swinging axe, taking hits, giant crit numbers exploding. Mood: reckless ecstasy.

cards.power: The party sends you into every room first. You believe this is honor.
cards.lore: A hero who solves problems by hitting them will be handed every problem.
cards.gradeReason: The trap-tester who thinks it's glory — pure performative delusion.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: honey badger barbarian proudly entering dark doorway, party pointing with relieved smiles. Mood: noble oblivion.

cards.power: You rage again. There was no cooldown anyway.
cards.lore: At high enough level, the barbarian stops being a character and beco[m—text clipped at page edge]
cards.gradeReason: Infinite rage, zero cooldown — this is a force of nature playing a game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink red-black. Subject: honey badger barbarian as whirling vortex of destruction, debris everywhere. Mood: elemental, unstoppable.

cards.power: You throw a tiny magic dart. You have four hit points.
cards.lore: The wizard begins as the smartest person in the room and the easiest to kill.
cards.gradeReason: Tiny dart + four HP is the most recognizable wizard experience possible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink blue-wash. Subject: owl wizard with glowing finger-dart, giant rhino fighter beside him like a bodyguard. Mood: fragile genius.

cards.power: You have the perfect spell for this. You used it last encounter.
cards.lore: A wizard's power is infinite, in theory, once per day.
cards.gradeReason: The empty spellbook moment — every wizard player lives this.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: owl wizard holding open spellbook stamped USED, monsters closing in. Mood: horrified regret.

cards.power: You correct the DM on the lore. You are right. It does not help.
cards.lore: Knowing exactly how the world works is not the same as surviving it.
cards.gradeReason: Rules lawyer in a crisis — table recognizes this immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: owl wizard lecturing at chalkboard mid-combat, party fighting monsters behind him. Mood: detached pedantry.

cards.power: You end the encounter in one spell. You also end yourself in one hit.
cards.lore: At high level the wizard is a god, between naps.
cards.gradeReason: God or corpse, no middle ground — classic high-level wizard experience.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink blue explosive. Subject: owl wizard unleashing massive spell, one enemy arrow already en route to end him. Mood: magnificent fragility.

cards.power: You did magic. You don't know how. You did not study.
cards.lore: The wizard earned it. The sorcerer woke up with it and never let the wizard forget.
cards.gradeReason: Innate magic with zero effort — the smugness is immediately performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink pink-fire. Subject: lemur sorcerer in casual clothes, magic exploding off hands, shocked expression. Mood: accidental magnificence.

cards.power: You cast a spell. The DM rolls on a table. Everyone holds their breath.
cards.lore: Innate power comes with innate consequences and no instruction manual.
cards.gradeReason: Collective breath-hold is a full-table performance every session.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink chaotic. Subject: lemur sorcerer casting, colorful chaos explosion around them, party diving for cover. Mood: delightful panic.

cards.power: You out-cast the wizard while eating. The wizard files a complaint.
cards.lore: Talent is the only thing more annoying than the person who has it.
cards.gradeReason: Effortless superiority while eating — the wizard's nightmare perfectly cast.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: lemur sorcerer munching food and blasting spells, owl wizard scribbling angry complaint letter. Mood: infuriating ease.

cards.power: You reshape the spell mid-cast. It might fireball the party.
cards.lore: Raw power never asked permission and never reads the room.
cards.gradeReason: Friendly fire threat as party performance — instantly recognizable chaos.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: lemur sorcerer mid-metamagic twist, party scrambling away, fireball forming. Mood: chaotic bravado.

cards.power: You wanted to fight. The party voted you the healer.
cards.lore: Nobody chooses to be the medic. The party chooses for them.
cards.gradeReason: Unwanted healer role is every cleric's origin story — immediately embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink gold-wash. Subject: capybara cleric receiving healer kit against their will, giant divine hand pressing it on them. Mood: resigned sacrifice.

cards.power: You heal the loudest first. Volume is not the same as injury.
cards.lore: A healer learns whom to save by who screams the most convincingly.
cards.gradeReason: Observational truth — defines behavior but less a direct performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: capybara cleric tending to screaming raccoon, unconscious badger unnoticed nearby. Mood: chaotic triage.

cards.power: You heal the rogue. You make sure the rogue knows how you feel about it.
cards.lore: Divine mercy comes with a free divine opinion.
cards.gradeReason: Healing with commentary is a full roleplay performance — zero setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: capybara cleric healing raccoon rogue with deeply disapproving side-eye. Mood: begrudging divinity.

cards.power: You are out of spells. The party turns to you anyway.
cards.lore: Everyone forgets the cleric exists until the exact moment they need her.
cards.gradeReason: Invisible until needed — a perfect table dynamic every cleric player has lived.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: capybara cleric surrounded by desperate party members, empty spellbook open, resigned calm. Mood: quiet indispensability.

cards.power: You identify every plant. You eat the wrong one anyway.
cards.lore: The druid knows the forest intimately and trusts it completely, which is the problem.
cards.gradeReason: Poisoned by own expertise — immediately playable druid irony.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink green. Subject: opossum druid confidently eating glowing mushroom, party wincing. Mood: informed recklessness.

cards.power: You turn into a bear. You will be solving most problems as a bear now.
cards.lore: Give a druid one animal form and every encounter becomes that animal.
cards.gradeReason: Bear = solution to everything — the most iconic druid one-trick ever.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: half-transformed opossum-bear, party pointing at problems with LET THE BEAR sign. Mood: universal bear solution.

cards.power: You stop the raid to explain why the dungeon is unsustainable.
cards.lore: No one invited the lecture. The lecture comes free with the nature magic.
cards.gradeReason: Sustainability speech mid-dungeon — a scene that plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: bear-druid lecturing at torch about fire hazards, frustrated adventurers sitting. Mood: preachy magnificence.

cards.power: You have not been a person in three sessions. The party has stopped asking.
cards.lore: A druid who can be anything will, eventually, just be the bear.
cards.gradeReason: Three sessions as a bear — the table has fully accepted it. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: large bear at campfire with party toasting marshmallows, everyone comfortable. Mood: inevitable acceptance.

cards.power: You check every door, chest, and floor tile for traps. The party waits.
cards.lore: The rogue's first level is mostly the party standing in a hallway.
cards.gradeReason: Party-waiting is a situation, not yet a performance invitation for the player.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: raccoon rogue with magnifying glass on floor tile, impatient party behind. Mood: methodical paranoia.

cards.power: You stab it once for damage the fighter dreams about.
cards.lore: The rogue does nothing for five rounds and then settles the whole fight.
cards.gradeReason: Five rounds of nothing then nuclear hit — rogue's defining performance arc.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: tiny raccoon rogue emerging from shadows, 999 DMG explosion, fighter jaw dropping. Mood: delayed devastation.

cards.power: You loot the body before the party reaches it. You looted the party too.
cards.lore: A rogue does not distinguish between enemy pockets and friendly ones.
cards.gradeReason: Friend-or-foe looting — a full characterization you live into immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: raccoon rogue rifling enemy pockets with one hand, lifting capybara's purse with other. Mood: cheerful criminality.

cards.cardName: The I Was Never Here Rogue
cards.power: You vanish before the consequences arrive. The blame lands on the bard.
cards.lore: The perfect heist leaves no evidence, only a confused bard.
cards.gradeReason: Vanish + bard takes blame — two character performances in one card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: peacock bard holding stolen crown with question marks, raccoon rogue invisible, guards approaching. Mood: perfect deniability.

cards.power: You read the trail. You know what passed, when, and how it felt about it.
cards.lore: The ranger sees a story in the mud that no one asked him to narrate.
cards.gradeReason: Narrating mud stories to uninterested party — observational, needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink green. Subject: wolf ranger nose-down on trail, party impatiently waiting, ranger giving dramatic exposition. Mood: unsolicited expertise.

cards.power: You chose goblins as your sworn nemesis at character creation.
cards.lore: A ranger prepares perfectly for the one enemy he will never meet.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect preparation for the enemy that never shows — pure tragicomic roleplay.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: wolf ranger holding GOBLINS sign confidently, massive dragon looming behind. Mood: misplaced certainty.

cards.power: You have no idea how to talk to a shopkeeper. You offer to track him instead.
cards.lore: The wilderness expert becomes furniture the moment there is a roof.
cards.gradeReason: Tracking offer to shopkeeper — a scene that writes itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: wolf ranger crouched reading shopkeeper's footprints, confused shopkeeper staring. Mood: spectacular social failure.

cards.power: Your animal companion does the cool thing. Everyone pets the wolf. Not you.
cards.lore: The ranger spent four levels becoming the second most interesting member of his own duo.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone pets the wolf, not you — a three-word heartbreak you live into.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: glowing spirit wolf surrounded by adoring party, wolf ranger standing aside unloved. Mood: dignified irrelevance.

cards.power: You perform for the tavern. Some of them even wanted you to.
cards.lore: Every bard's career begins with an audience that did not consent.
cards.gradeReason: Non-consensual tavern performance — the bard's founding myth, fully playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink rosy. Subject: peacock bard performing on crate, half tavern rapt, other half clearly unwilling. Mood: oblivious enthusiasm.

cards.power: You tell the fighter he's doing great. The fighter rolls better. Science cannot explain it.
cards.lore: The bard's true magic is making other people slightly more confident than they should be.
cards.gradeReason: Cheerleader magic that inexplicably works — pure bard performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: peacock bard gesturing encouragingly at glowing rhino fighter, dice rolling natural 20. Mood: inexplicable encouragement.

cards.power: You attempt to romance the quest-giver, the villain, and the dragon. In that order.
cards.lore: The bard has never met a plot he could not complicate with flirtation.
cards.gradeReason: The bard who seduces everyone including the dragon — table legend fuel.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: peacock bard offering heart-scroll to blushing dragon, owl and rhino facepalming. Mood: catastrophic romance.

cards.power: You write the ballad of the campaign. You are the hero of every verse.
cards.lore: History is written by the bard, which is why the bard always wins it.
cards.gradeReason: Self-authored heroism — the bard's endgame play, fully embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: peacock bard in full-feather spotlight, tiny stick-figure party in background of his ballad. Mood: spectacular ego.

cards.power: You take the oath. You mean every word with your whole heart.
cards.lore: The paladin's oath is the most sincere thing at a table built on lying to a DM.
cards.gradeReason: Total sincerity in a room of chaos — immediately and perfectly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink gold. Subject: lion paladin kneeling at altar in golden light, eyes closed in total conviction. Mood: earnest holiness.

cards.power: You pour every spell slot into one holy hit. The undead simply leaves.
cards.lore: The paladin saves it all up for one righteous moment and spends it loudly.
cards.gradeReason: Saving everything for one massive smite — the paladin's defining ecstasy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink explosive gold. Subject: lion paladin unleashing apocalyptic divine smite, skeleton disintegrating mid-wave. Mood: righteous overkill.

cards.power: You remind the party that stealing is wrong. The party was mid-steal.
cards.lore: Every party gets the conscience it deserves and none of them wanted.
cards.gradeReason: Ethics interruption mid-heist — a scene that plays itself at every table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: lion paladin blocking door with raised paw as raccoon rogue and bard freeze mid-steal. Mood: unwelcome righteousness.

cards.power: You found a loophole in your own oath. You are still good. Mostly.
cards.lore: The longer the oath holds, the more creative the holding becomes.
cards.gradeReason: Divine loophole lawyering — a full character arc in one sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: lion paladin annotating sacred oath scroll with asterisks and footnotes, halo slightly tilted. Mood: creative righteousness.

cards.power: You have no armor and no weapon. You have a philosophy and bad feet.
cards.lore: The monk arrives at the dungeon dressed for a completely different occasion.
cards.gradeReason: Dressed wrong for the dungeon — the monk's first-level identity in full.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: heron monk in meditation robe at dungeon entrance, armored party staring in confusion. Mood: serene inappropriateness.

cards.power: You punch four times in the time it takes the fighter to swing once.
cards.lore: Nobody respected the punching class until the punching started.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanical description — states what you do more than inviting you to be it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink orange. Subject: heron/fox monk as spinning blur of fists, fighter frozen mid-one-swing. Mood: ridiculous speed.

cards.power: You deflect the arrow, walk on the water, and say something cryptic.
cards.lore: The monk spends the whole campaign being a surprise to people who read his sheet.
cards.gradeReason: Campaign-long mystery surprise — a roleplay posture you inhabit from session one.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: heron monk standing on water surface, deflected arrow mid-air, party gobsmacked. Mood: quiet revelation.

cards.power: You punch the dragon. The dragon was not built for this matchup.
cards.lore: At high level there is no problem the monk cannot solve by hitting it with his hands specifically.
cards.gradeReason: Punching the dragon — the monk's entire high-level arc in one moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: tiny heron monk punching dragon directly in face, dragon visibly surprised. Mood: absurd triumph.

cards.power: You sign the deal for power. You skim the terms.
cards.lore: The warlock got everything everything he wanted and one clause he did not read.
cards.gradeReason: Sign now, regret clause later — instant warlock origin performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink purple. Subject: goat warlock eagerly signing tentacle-sealed contract, Cthulhu-patron grinning behind. Mood: enthusiastic mistake.

cards.power: You fire the same beam again. You will fire it every turn forever.
cards.lore: Give a warlock one good attack and he will never learn another.
cards.gradeReason: One-button forever — the warlock's eternal commitment, immediately embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: goat warlock firing identical eldritch beam, surrounded by untouched spellbook pages. Mood: committed simplicity.

cards.power: Your patron whispers a side-quest mid-dungeon. You cannot say no.
cards.lore: Power on loan comes with a landlord who visits without warning.
cards.gradeReason: Mid-dungeon patron interruption — a scene you cannot not play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: goat warlock frozen mid-fight, glowing patron-eye in corner issuing demands. Mood: captive helplessness.

cards.power: Your patron arrives to collect. You are now part of the dungeon.
cards.lore: Every warlock learns the same lesson on the last page of the contract.
cards.gradeReason: Patron arrives to collect — the warlock's ultimate end-game, inescapably performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink purple. Subject: goat warlock being absorbed into dungeon wall by massive tentacles. Mood: inevitable consequence.

cards.power: You loot the cemetery for parts. You call it research.
cards.lore: The necromancer's hobby is everyone else's nightmare and he cannot understand why.
cards.gradeReason: Calling grave robbery research — cheerful necromancer oblivion, fully playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: vulture necromancer whistling while collecting skull from cemetery at night. Mood: cheerfully oblivious horror.

cards.power: You raise your first skeleton. You named it. You are attached now.
cards.lore: A necromancer's first creation is the first friend who could not leave.
cards.gradeReason: Named skeleton attachment — a relationship you inhabit immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: vulture necromancer adjusting bow tie on beloved skeleton, MY BOY expression of pride. Mood: macabre tenderness.

cards.power: You bring your skeletons to the tavern. The party sits at the other table.
cards.lore: The necromancer is the only class whose party-balance problem is social.
cards.gradeReason: Social exclusion via skeleton entourage — a scene that plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: vulture necromancer and skeleton crew at tavern table, rest of party at far corner. Mood: blissfully excluded.

cards.power: You command two hundred undead. You have never been more alone.
cards.lore: A man who builds his own company has only the company he built.
cards.gradeReason: Two hundred undead, zero friends — the necromancer's existential peak.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: small vulture necromancer silhouette on hill commanding vast undead army, utterly alone. Mood: magnificent loneliness.

cards.power: You write forty pages of lore. The players will read none of it.
cards.lore: Every DM begins by mistaking the module for the campaign.
cards.gradeReason: Forty pages unread — every DM's foundational wound, immediately lived.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit buried under lore notes, players ignoring stack of papers. Mood: devoted futility.

cards.power: The players go left. Everything you prepared was to the right. You smile and invent a town.
cards.lore: A DM's real skill is named "yes, and" and learned the hard way.
cards.gradeReason: Invent a town mid-panic — the improvising DM's defining performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink golden. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit gesturing wildly, inventing town behind players who went the wrong way. Mood: creative panic.

cards.power: You feel the urge to force the plot. You resist. Mostly.
cards.lore: The hardest roll a DM makes is the one against his own outline.
cards.gradeReason: Resist railroading. Mostly. — the DM's eternal inner conflict in one word.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit with devil on shoulder pointing at PLOT arrow, angel pleading for player freedom. Mood: tempted restraint.

cards.power: You set the table. The players arrive. You do not pretend to know what happens next.
cards.lore: Stay fluffy.
cards.gradeReason: Poetic and true but 'Stay fluffy' is mantra, not a clear performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor ink warm. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit serene at empty table, mystical cards laid out, firelight, infinite possibility. Mood: open invitation.

verdict: The full class roster is the dungeon raid deck everyone at every TTRPG table has already lived — they just haven't played it with cards yet. Fifty out of fifty-six cards are pure Grade 1 character embodiments; the writing is economical, surgical, and funny in the way that only accuracy can be funny. The one structural weakness is the Weather-Event Barbarian lore being clipped at the page edge. Otherwise this is table-ready in every sense. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: Thirteen classes. Four levels each. You have played all of them. The D&D deck that makes everyone at the table say 'oh god that's me.'

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — Four-panel comic with FrizzleBob D20, class cards fanned, dungeon door — tight and iconic
coverQA.coverTitle: 4 — 'Plato's Dungeon Raid' is intriguing; Plato + dungeon contrast works well
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Cover promise ('you have played all of them') matches deck delivery exactly
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Classic 2x2 Kayfabizarro signature format executed sharply
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — 'Bring Your Own Legend' and 'You have played all of them' are both quotable
coverQA.coverNote: Cover is a masterclass in promise-delivery alignment. The bottom taglines front-load the joke before a single card is seen. FrizzleBob's smirk with the D20 is the perfect host face for this material.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 card pages (2x2 grid). All 13 D&D classes x4 cards = 52 + 4 FrizzleBob DM cards = 56 total. Animal casting consistent throughout: Rhino=Fighter, HoneyBadger=Barbarian, Owl=Wizard, Lemur=Sorcerer, Capybara=Cleric, Opossum/Bear=Druid, Raccoon=Rogue, Wolf=Ranger, Peacock=Bard, Lion=Paladin, Heron/Crane=Monk, Goat=Warlock, Vulture=Necromancer, FrizzleBob=DM. All text legible. One lore text clipped at page edge: Weather-Event Barbarian card 8, lore stops at 'becom'. No font artifacts. This is v05 of the third Plato's Dungeon Raid deck — the polished full-roster version. Cover tagline 'Thirteen classes. Four levels each.' is the structural key; each class page delivers exactly 4 variants of escalating or diverging play style.

Class name headers currently only appear as page titles — subtle card design element could reinforce class identity

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: PLATO'S DUNGEON RAID – You Have Played Every One of These (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

You have played all thirteen classes. You have never once admitted which one is actually you.

Plato swore the truest version of any thing lived in some perfect realm, clean and far from the folding table. He died without ever rolling a level-three Warlock who skimmed the contract. So here is the real ideal form of the party: the Fighter who read none of the rulebook and showed up on time, the Wizard with one spell and four hit points, the Druid who has not been a person in three sessions. Not heroes. Recognitions. You met every one of them over cold pizza, and you have been quietly being one of them ever since.

This is Social Story Wrestling dragged to the dungeon door. You draw a class, you commit to the bit out loud, and the table rules whether you sold it or got booked straight back behind the screen. Thirteen classes, four cards each, plus the rabbit running the whole game.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Full Class Roster Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The I Seduce It Bard, The Permanently-A-Bear Druid, and The Pact-Came-Due Warlock.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and four escalating levels per class so the bit climbs from first-day rookie to full weather event.
- The Animal Casting Bench: every class wears a beast, Rhino Fighter, Owl Wizard, Vulture Necromancer, FrizzleBob on the DM throne, so the archetype reads across the table before a single word is spoken.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
By grabbing this roster you enter the Plato's Dungeon Raid pipeline. Future sets in the cycle, the Hero builds, the Monster Codex, the campaign expansions, all land in your library as free updates. Buy the table once, keep getting the dungeon.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I spent too long on the wrong side of the DM screen learning that the characters people love are never the legendary ones. They are the ones everybody recognizes. This deck is that recognition, cut and ready to deal tonight. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, run it at your next session. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next set of cards.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The ideal form of the hero was never up in the heavens. It was the one who pressed the button that makes the numbers bigger."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
